title: Day-trader mode: genericize the portfolio risk/exit/profit-target layer's hard-coded weekly/daily split
description:
Follow-up split out of backend-day-trader-timeframe-mode-signal-engine's own checklist item 1 (see that task's `decisions` entry for the full scope-split rationale): that task genericized `app.signals.triple_screen`/`app.signals.engine`'s Screen 1-3 + Impulse + confidence pipeline to operate over whichever `TimeframeTriple` is currently active, but deliberately left `app.portfolio.risk`/`app.portfolio.profit_target`/`app.portfolio.exits` untouched -- these still unconditionally assume swing mode's weekly/daily split regardless of `TradingMode`.

Specifically, still hard-coded today:

- `app.portfolio.risk.protective_stop`'s SafeZone-style stop uses `_SWING_LOW_WINDOW_DAYS` (10 *trading days*, ~2 calendar weeks) as its swing-low lookback window -- meaningless as a literal day-count once the active intermediate/short-term timeframe is intraday (e.g. what does '10 trading days' mean when watching 2-minute bars?). Needs a real methodology decision: a bar-count window scaled to whichever timeframe is active, a wall-clock-duration window resolved generically per `TimeframeInterval`, or something else -- not a mechanical rename.
- `app.portfolio.profit_target.suggest_profit_target`'s channel candidate is explicitly computed from the *weekly* chart (ch. 39 p.161's 'the value zone on a weekly chart presents a good target', per docs/Analyse.md §7's 'Swing-style' profit-target section) -- needs deciding whether day-trader mode's profit target should instead read the active triple's own long-term leg (matching ch. 39's literal 'set profit targets using long-term charts' framing generalized) or whether this rule is swing-mode-specific by design and should simply not apply (or apply differently) in day-trader mode.
- `app.portfolio.exits.evaluate_exit_flags`'s `'tide_flipped_bearish'` flag reads `weekly_ohlcv` directly (a required parameter, not sourced from `app.signals.engine.analyse_day_trader`) -- needs to read whichever data plays the long-term/Tide role for the active mode instead.

Needs an `elder-signal-reviewer` pass before merge, same as its parent task, given this directly touches the 6% Rule/protective-stop risk logic docs/Analyse.md §7 documents and ch. 39 p.161's own long-term-chart profit-target framing.

checklist.step: Decide (and record via `decisions`) how `_SWING_LOW_WINDOW_DAYS`-style bar-count windows should generalize across timeframes -- a fixed bar count regardless of timeframe, a wall-clock-duration-derived count per `TimeframeInterval`, or something else.
Decide (and record via `decisions`) whether `suggest_profit_target`'s weekly-chart channel candidate reads the active triple's long-term leg in day-trader mode, or is scoped to swing mode only.

Genericize `app.portfolio.risk.protective_stop`, `app.portfolio.profit_target.suggest_profit_target`, and `app.portfolio.exits.evaluate_exit_flags` per the decisions above, with swing mode's existing behavior preserved exactly (regression tests, not just new-behavior tests).
Unit/integration tests for the generic risk/exit/profit-target evaluation under day-trader mode, including a mocked IBKR intraday provider where relevant.
elder-signal-reviewer pass before merge -- confirm the 6% Rule/protective-stop/profit-target logic still matches docs/Analyse.md §7 once genericized.
Update docs/architecture/Backend.md §10's 'Not yet landed' list accordingly.

decisions.decision: `_SWING_LOW_WINDOW_DAYS` (renamed to `_SWING_LOW_WINDOW_BARS`, value unchanged at 10) generalizes across timeframes as a FIXED BAR COUNT, not a wall-clock-duration-derived one. `app.portfolio.risk.protective_stop`'s `daily_ohlcv` parameter is left un-renamed (matching `app.signals.engine.analyse`'s own `daily_ohlcv`/`weekly_ohlcv` precedent) but is now explicitly documented as timeframe-agnostic: it plays whichever OHLCV fills the *intermediate* role for the active trading mode (ch. 39 p.161: stops live on the intermediate timeframe's own chart in either mode), so the 10-bar SafeZone lookback is '10 bars of whichever timeframe is actually being traded on' -- literal daily bars for swing mode (unchanged), or day-trader mode's own intermediate leg (e.g. 10 bars of a 10-minute leg = ~100 minutes) once a future caller wires that leg through. `app.portfolio.profit_target.suggest_profit_target`'s own `weekly_ohlcv` parameter (renamed internal helper `_weekly_channel_bounds` -> `_long_term_channel_bounds`, parameter itself left un-renamed for the same reason) generalizes the same way to whichever OHLCV fills the *long-term* role, and now reads day-trader mode's `long_term` leg once wired -- see the next decision entry for the fuller rationale on that specific question. No functional code change to any of the three genericized functions was needed for either decision: `protective_stop`'s `.tail(N)` window was already a positional (bar-count) slice, and `_long_term_channel_bounds`/`evaluate_exit_flags`'s `tide_flipped_bearish` flag (via `evaluate_tide`) were already plain `pd.DataFrame`-agnostic passes with no calendar-week-specific logic anywhere in their own implementations -- this task's actual work was confirming that genericity is real (not assumed) via new discriminating tests, documenting it explicitly (the old names/docstrings described only swing mode's own usage, which read as a hard requirement rather than the incidental case it always was), and deciding the bar-count-vs-wall-clock-duration question this checklist item calls out as a genuine judgment call.
decisions.rationale: A wall-clock-duration-derived window (translating '10 trading days' into a per-leg bar count via `TimeframeInterval.approx_trading_minutes`, e.g. 10 trading days = 3900 minutes = 390 bars of a 10-minute leg) was considered and rejected: a day trader's whole position lifecycle is typically intraday (minutes to hours), so a swing-low/volatility-buffer lookback spanning a wall-clock month of 10-minute bars would smear the 'recent' concept this stop exists to measure across far more history than is relevant to that trader's own holding period -- the SafeZone stop would end up reacting to volatility from weeks ago instead of the last few hours, defeating its own purpose. A fixed bar count, by contrast, naturally scales DOWN as the active intermediate leg's granularity gets finer (10 bars of a 25-minute leg = ~4.2 trading hours, roughly a session; 10 bars of a 10-minute leg = ~1.7 hours; 10 bars of daily bars = ~2 weeks, swing mode's own unchanged case) -- this tracks Elder's actual intent (a *recent* swing low/volatility measure, calibrated to whichever timeframe the trader is currently working on) far better than translating the literal '10 trading days' wall-clock figure, which was itself only ever this app's own swing-mode-specific judgment call (see the pre-existing `portfolio-risk-rules` task's `decisions` entry), not a number from the book that needs preserving in wall-clock terms across timeframes. This mirrors `_WAVE_LOOKBACK_BARS`'s own identical bar-count-not-day-count precedent, already established and reviewed by `backend-day-trader-timeframe-mode-signal-engine`. Also confirmed there is no genuinely distinct 'something else' option worth choosing over these two: a per-timeframe-tuned constant table was considered and rejected as unwarranted complexity for a single already-documented judgment-call number, with no evidence from docs/Analyse.md or ch. 39/54 that the SafeZone window should vary by anything other than what a fixed bar count already captures.

decisions.decision: `suggest_profit_target`'s weekly-chart channel candidate (`_long_term_channel_bounds`, renamed from `_weekly_channel_bounds`) generalizes to read the active triple's `long_term` leg in day-trader mode -- it is NOT scoped to swing mode only. `evaluate_exit_flags`'s `tide_flipped_bearish` flag generalizes the identical way: it reads whichever data fills the long-term/Tide role for the active mode, via its own (un-renamed) `weekly_ohlcv` parameter.
decisions.rationale: Ch. 39 p.161, read directly (already quoted in this module's own docstring and docs/Analyse.md §7): 'Triple Screen calls for setting profit targets using long-term charts and stops on the charts of your intermediate timeframe' -- a genuinely generic rule about the long-term/intermediate SPLIT, not a rule specifically about calendar weeks vs. calendar days; this app's swing-mode mapping (long-term=weekly) is one instance of that generic rule, not the rule itself, exactly as `app.signals.engine.analyse_day_trader` already established for Screen 1/Tide (`long_term_ohlcv` plays the Tide role in day-trader mode the same way `weekly_ohlcv` does in swing mode) and for `evaluate_exit_flags`'s own `tide_flipped_bearish` flag, which is a direct `evaluate_tide` call on the same data. Scoping either rule to 'swing mode only' would have required inventing a NEW, swing-specific carve-out with no textual support -- the opposite of what ch. 39 actually says -- and would leave day-trader mode's profit-target/exit-flag logic silently reading the wrong (or no) long-term data once a future caller wires day-trader-mode inputs through these functions, a worse outcome than a consistent generic rule. The alternative -- that day-trader mode should have NO profit-target-channel concept at all, given the book's separate third (day-trade-specific) profit-target technique this module explicitly doesn't implement (see this module's own docstring) -- was also considered: rejected because that third technique is about a *different exit signal* (first sign of opposing divergence), not a claim that the long-term-chart value-zone technique stops applying once a trader's *timeframes* happen to be intraday; ch. 39's day-trading examples still have a long-term leg (just a faster one), and nothing in the text suggests the value-zone target technique becomes inapplicable once that leg is measured in minutes rather than weeks. As with the sibling decision above, this is a decision about what these functions are now CAPABLE of, not a claim that day-trader-mode data is wired through either of `suggest_profit_target`'s two real callers or `evaluate_exit_flags`'s one real caller today -- both callers (`GET /api/stocks/{ticker}/analysis`, `GET /api/portfolio/risk`) still always pass literal daily/weekly bars regardless of the active trading mode, per `docs/architecture/Backend.md` §10's 'Not yet landed' list (that wiring, plus the per-position-day-trader-mode-fetch latency question it raises, is `backend-day-trader-timeframe-mode-api-followups`'s job, not this task's).

decisions.decision: Checklist item 5 ('elder-signal-reviewer pass before merge') is left unchecked by task-worker despite running the `verify-elder-signal` skill's own checklist as a rigorous self-review pass during implementation (per this task's `skill` field and its dispatch instruction to apply that skill's rigor throughout): confirmed the 2%/6% rules still read current equity/current position risk (both untouched by this task), `evaluate_exit_flags` still takes no `signal` parameter (existing regression test `test_hold_signal_is_irrelevant_the_function_takes_no_signal_input` still passes unchanged), and the protective-stop formula is still `swing_low - (coefficient * volatility_buffer)` with no functional change -- only `_SWING_LOW_WINDOW_DAYS`/`_weekly_channel_bounds` renamed and docstrings generalized. Also mutation-tested every new discriminating test added by this task (temporarily reverted the genericization framing in a scratch copy of each of the three modules -- widening the SafeZone window, swapping `_long_term_channel_bounds`'s daily/weekly argument, and swapping `evaluate_exit_flags`'s weekly-role data source to `daily_ohlcv` -- confirmed each new test fails under the corresponding regression, then restored the file and confirmed the full suite passes again) rather than trusting the tests pass without checking they'd actually catch the regression they claim to guard against. Left the checklist item itself unchecked because 'elder-signal-reviewer pass' names a specific, distinct pipeline step (the `elder-signal-reviewer` read-only audit agent, dispatched by `pr-reviewer` against this PR) rather than a self-review task-worker can complete on its own behalf -- checking it off here would misrepresent that a different agent's independent pass already happened.
decisions.rationale: CLAUDE.md's task-worker instructions say to check off a checklist item 'only once you've actually verified them, same bar task-qa-reviewer holds' -- task-worker verifying its own work is real verification for an ordinary implementation checklist item, but this specific item names a named agent (`elder-signal-reviewer`) as part of the PR review pipeline (CLAUDE.md's Agents section: 'read-only audit of trading logic ... loads the verify-elder-signal skill'), the same way `backend-day-trader-timeframe-mode-signal-engine`'s own PR #312 review history shows this pass actually happening during `pr-reviewer`'s dispatch, not during `task-worker`'s own implementation turn. Marking it done here would be indistinguishable, to a later reader of this task's checklist, from that independent agent pass having already occurred -- exactly the kind of self-graded checklist item CLAUDE.md's review pipeline is designed to avoid. The substantive methodology work itself (Analyse.md §7 grounding, the two genuine judgment calls, mutation-tested discriminating tests) is done regardless of who formally checks this box; leaving it open just accurately reflects that the formal independent pass is still pending.
